did.unittitle: Brooklyn, New York, N.Y. Borough Park Congregational Church records, 1913-1936.
did.abstract: The Borough Park Congregational Church in Brooklyn, New York, was established in 1903. A church building was constructed at the corners of 49th street and Fort Hamilton Parkway circa 1910. The church was dissolved in 1936. This collection contains two volumes of trustees and executive board records that include meeting minutes and financial records.

custodhist.head: Custodial History
custodhist.p: Materials in this collection were given to the New York Conference of the United Church of Christ at an unknown time, likely following the church's dissolution. This collection was originally processed as part of the New York Conference records (RG0112) circa 1980.

bioghist.head: Historical Note
bioghist.p: The Borough Park Congregational Church in Brooklyn, New York, was established in 1903. Rev. Elliott Darling was the church's first minister. A church building was constructed at the corners of 49th street and Fort Hamilton Parkway circa 1910. Lightning struck the church in 1916, damaging the cupola. The church was dissolved in 1936. The building was sold to Rabbi Shlomo Chaim (Herbert) Port who converted the church into the Borough Park Synagogue. The building was destroyed in a fire in 1941.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This collection contains two volumes of records from the Borough Park Congregational Church in Brooklyn, New York. The volumes largely contain meeting minutes and financial records related to the trustees and the executive board of the church.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Materials in this collection have been arranged into chronological order by start date.
